title: Learned wing sensing supports damage detection and lift recovery in a flapping robot
summary: A prototype flapping-wing robot used integrated wing sensors with a learned Kriging surrogate to reconstruct wing motion and a linear SVM to classify damaged states. The SVM achieved 94.6% accuracy on 168 held-out samples, and a separate damaged-wing bench demonstration increased flapping frequency within 0.1 seconds to restore average lift near the intact baseline. These are device-specific physical sensing and control results, with calibration and comparison against binocular-vision measurements. They do not establish autonomous free-flight performance, generalization across robot designs or sustained field operation.
ai_technology: Physics-informed Kriging surrogate model and linear support vector machine (SVM)
organization: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China; City University of Hong Kong; The University of Tokyo

evidence.tested: The Kriging model was calibrated using two signal cycles and evaluated on other cycles at each frequency against binocular-vision measurements; reported mean unit-pitching-angle error was below 10% and maximum flapping-angle error 1.1%. For fault diagnosis, 504 samples trained a linear SVM and 168 test samples yielded 94.6% accuracy across normal and three failure states. The authors also report a damaged-wing feedback demonstration with frequency rising from 12.9 to 19.3 Hz in 0.1 seconds and average lift restored near the intact baseline.
evidence.unknown: Generalization to other wing structures, sensor builds, operating conditions, and untethered flight; evidence for field deployment or sustained operational use.
evidence.ai_role: The physics-informed Kriging surrogate maps measured voltage/current amplitudes and flapping frequency to wing-motion angles; a linear SVM classifies faults from the derived signal features. These learned operations support the experimentally demonstrated intrinsic motion sensing, fault classification and lift-compensation control.

source_review.scope: Original final-journal PMC/EuropePMC XML: learned Kriging/SVM operation, image-referenced wing-motion checks, train/test sample counts, damage-feedback lift results, device-calibration limitations, affiliations and date.
